recording_stop.description: Stop the current recording and process it. Returns the video path when complete.

recording_id.description: The recording ID to stop. If not provided, stops the active recording.

title.description: Short title for the recording (max 5 words).

report_blocker.name: report_blocker
report_blocker.description: Report operational blockers that impede Opulent's ability to perform. This tool is ONLY for issues that affect Opulent's ability to operate — NOT for bugs or issues you found in the user's code during your task.

headline.description: One-line summary of the blocker (always visible).

notify.description: Who should be notified: user, org_admin, or cognition.

impact.description: How much the issue affected this session. Defaults to soft_blocked.

severity.description: How urgent the fix is globally. Defaults to medium.

details.description: Markdown description of the blocker (expandable in UI).

recommended_action.description: What the notified party should do to resolve this.

tags.description: Freeform tags for Datadog faceting and trend analysis.

request_secret.name: request_secret
request_secret.description: Request a secret from the user (e.g. API keys, passwords, TOTP codes). This will display a secure UI to the user where they can provide the secret value. The secret will be stored as an environment variable accessible in your shell.

secret_name.description: The name/key for the secret (e.g. VERCEL_LOGIN_PASSWORD, GITHUB_API_KEY, SLACK_2FA). This will be the environment variable name the secret is stored under.

type.description: The type of secret being requested. 'plain' for plain text secrets like API keys and passwords. 'totp' for TOTP/2FA authenticator secrets.

should_save.description: If true, the secret will be saved and available for future Opulent sessions (not just this session).

save_scope.description: The scope for saving the secret. Only relevant when should_save is true.

repo_name.description: The full qualified repository name to scope the secret to. Required when save_scope is 'repo'.

note.description: A short human-readable note explaining what this secret is for, so the user can identify it in future sessions.

sensitive.description: Whether the secret value should be treated as sensitive and masked in the UI. Defaults to true.

run_workflow.name: run_workflow
run_workflow.description: Run a dynamic workflow: a deterministic Python script that orchestrates multiple child Opulent sessions.

workflow_name.description: Descriptive name for this workflow run, e.g. 'review-fanout-v1'.

run_id.description: Run to resume: the run_id ("wfr-...") reported by a previous invocation. Its recorded completed agent() results replay and the rest retry with fresh child sessions. Omit to start a new run.

script_path.description: Absolute path (on your machine) to the file containing the workflow's Python source — e.g. a `workflow.py` saved alongside a skill. The file is read once when approval is requested, so the approved run executes byte-for-byte what was saved at that moment. To run an edited file, call this tool again: the new request replaces the pending prompt. The workflow runtime is prepended automatically; do not define agent/pipeline/parallel/log yourself.

timeout_secs.description: Wall-clock budget in seconds for the whole run (default and max 7 days).

save_browser_profile.name: save_browser_profile
save_browser_profile.description: Save the current browser profile (cookies, passwords, local storage, etc.) so it persists across future sessions. This zips the browser data directory and suggests an update to the organization-wide blueprint that restores the browser state at the start of every future session.

title.description: Short title for the suggestion (shown in the user's timeline).

summary.description: One-paragraph summary of why the profile is being saved.

scripted_tools.name: scripted_tools
scripted_tools.description: Run a Python script on the box that calls your other tools programmatically.

script.description: Python (python3) source code to execute on the box.

timeout_secs.description: Wall-clock budget in seconds for the whole script (default 280, max 7 days).

set_workflow_agent_soft_time_limit.name: set_workflow_agent_soft_time_limit
set_workflow_agent_soft_time_limit.description: Set the advisory soft time limit for one dynamic-workflow agent or a whole phase mid-run.

run_id.description: The live run containing the agent or phase.

soft_time_limit_minutes.description: New expected duration in minutes (1-60). A running agent's clock restarts from now.

agent_id.description: Agent result id to set. Exactly one of agent_id or phase.

phase.description: Phase whose agents — running, queued, and started later — take the new limit. Exactly one of agent_id or phase.

skill.name: skill
skill.description: Invoke or discover skills. Modes: 'invoke' (default) activates a skill by name, 'list' discovers skills registered in a project at the given path (scans skill directories like .agents/skills/ at the project root, does not recurse into subdirectories), and 'search' recursively scans for model-invocable skills under a given path and filters them by optional keywords. Skills provide context-specific g

command.description: The skill operation to perform. Defaults to 'invoke' if omitted.

skill.description: The name of the skill to invoke (required for 'invoke' command). Use one of the available skills listed in the system prompt.

path.description: Project path to discover skills in (required for 'list' and 'search' commands). Scans skill directories (e.g. .agents/skills/) at the project root; list does not recurse into subdirectories, while search does.

keywords.description: List of keywords to search for. Empty or omitted means include all skills.

keywords_mode.description: Controls whether all keywords or any keyword need to be present.

stop.name: stop
stop.description: Stop working on the current task. Call this tool when you are done and do not need to communicate anything to the user. If you DO need to send a final message, use message_user with block_on_user=true instead.

suggest_knowledge.name: suggest_knowledge
suggest_knowledge.description: Suggest a knowledge item to be created or updated. This tool sends a suggestion that appears in the session header. The user can review and approve the suggestion.

action.description: The action to perform: 'create' for a new knowledge item, 'update' for an existing one.

value.description: The content of the knowledge item. For create, this is the new item's body. For update, this is the proposed replacement body.

trigger.description: When this knowledge should be retrieved — the scope/trigger description (required for create).

knowledge_id.description: ID of the existing knowledge item to update (required for update).

suggest_save_secret.name: suggest_save_secret
suggest_save_secret.description: Suggest to the user that they save a secret so it persists for future Opulent sessions. This emits a prompt to the frontend where the user can choose to save the secret.

env_var_name.description: The environment variable name to save the secret under (e.g. GITHUB_API_KEY, VERCEL_TOKEN). The value is read from secret_file — you do not pass the plaintext value here.

save_scope.description: The scope for saving the secret.

repo_name.description: The full qualified repository name to scope the secret to. Required when save_scope is 'repo'.

note.description: A short human-readable note explaining what this secret is for, so the user can identify it in future sessions.

type.description: The type of secret. 'plain' for plain text secrets like API keys and passwords. 'totp' for TOTP/2FA authenticator secrets.

secret_file.description: Path to a file on the box containing the secret value. The file name must start with 'secret_to_upload_' followed by a unique id. The file is read and deleted automatically after this tool is called.

subject.description: A brief title in imperative form (e.g. "Fix authentication bug", "Run tests and build").

description.description: Detailed context: requirements, acceptance criteria, relevant files, and the planned approach.

active_form.description: Present-continuous form shown while the task is in progress (e.g. "Fixing authentication bug").

task_id.description: The ID of the task to fetch.
The ID of the task to update.

status.description: New status. Use "deleted" to remove a task created in error or no longer relevant.

active_form.description: New present-continuous form shown while in progress.

add_blocked_by.description: Task IDs that block this task (added to any existing ones).

add_blocks.description: Task IDs that this task blocks (added to any existing ones).

testing_agent.name: testing_agent
testing_agent.description: Hand off UI-driven testing to your testing agent.

message.description: A message to the testing agent. State what to test, the behaviors or acceptance criteria to verify, and any relevant setup or environment changes.

user_testing_request.description: The testing approval evidence: the sentence from the user's message that requests or approves this testing, quoted verbatim. Required on the first handoff.

todo_write.name: todo_write
todo_write.description: Use this tool to create and manage a structured task list for your current session. It tracks your progress and gives the user visibility into what you are working on.

todos.description: The updated list of todo items.

status.description: Current status of the todo item.

query.description: A natural language query describing the task or desired tool capability. This input is passed through tokenization, stemming, and stopword removal, so keep it focused and keyword-rich rather than writing a full sentence.

limit.description: Maximum number of ranked tools to return. Use lower values for a focused result or higher values to explore the catalog. Default value is 10.

upload_attachment.name: upload_attachment
upload_attachment.description: Upload a file from the box to cloud storage and get a URL. Use this tool when you need to get a file's URL before referencing it elsewhere, such as embedding images in generated HTML or documents. Do not use this tool just to share files with the user — pass file paths to message_user's attachments parameter instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file on the box to upload. The file will be uploaded to cloud storage and a URL will be returned.

file_paths.description: A list of absolute file paths on the box to upload. Use this instead of file_path when uploading multiple files at once.

wait.name: wait
wait.description: Wait before continuing. Use this for non-event-driven delays like loading browser windows, or other cases where there is no specific signal to wait on. Pass seconds for a bounded wait (max 600). The wait ends early if an external event (e.g. a user message) arrives. Prefer this tool over running sleep in the shell — unlike sleep, this wait is cancelled the moment new input arrives.

seconds.description: Number of seconds to wait. Must be positive. Values above 600 are clamped to 600.

message.description: A concise explanation (no more than 10 words) of why the wait is needed.

web_get_contents.name: web_get_contents
web_get_contents.description: Fetch the full contents of one or more web pages by URL. Use this when you need to read the full text of a specific web page or extract content from multiple URLs at once (max 10).

urls.description: List of URLs to fetch content from (max 10).

web_search.name: web_search
web_search.description: Search the web for information using a search query. Returns relevant web page titles, URLs, and summaries. Use this when you need to find information online. You must not include extraneous information in web searches.

query.description: The search query to find relevant web pages. Keep the search string simple and focused.

num_results.description: Maximum number of results to return. Defaults to 5.

domain.description: Optional domain to restrict search results to (e.g. 'docs.rs').

write.name: write
write.description: Write content to a file, creating it if needed and overwriting it if it exists. Use this tool to create new files or for complete rewrites. If overwriting an existing file, you SHOULD use the read tool first to read the file's contents. NEVER proactively create documentation files (*.md) or README files unless explicitly requested. Only use emojis if the user explicitly requests them. Avoid writin

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write

content.description: The content to write to the file

write_to_process.name: write_to_process
write_to_process.description: Writes input to an interactive process running in a shell with support for both text and special characters. This command will NOT work if there is no command running in the shell. If you want to execute a command in the shell use the exec tool. Provide exactly ONE of text_input or bytes_input (never both).

shell_id.description: The ID of the shell to write to.

text_input.description: Text content to write to the shell (interpreted as literal text).

bytes_input.description: Special characters/bytes to write to the shell (interpreted with angle bracket notation).
